Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Herbst. The northern Gulf Coast is starting
to clean up after Hurricane Isaias left hundreds of thousands of customers without electricity.
The storm left at least two people dead, one in Florida and one in Alabama.
NPR's Debbie Elliott reports the storm made landfall last night near Destin,
Florida as a category two hurricane. Hurricane Isaias came ashore with 105 mile an hour winds,
a five foot storm surge and heavy rainfall, causing damage from the Alabama Gulf Coast
into the Florida panhandle. Florida Governor Ron DeSantis says emergency crews are working now
to clear down trees and power lines and repair damaged water systems.
It's still a very hazardous situation. All the assets are there to get the power back on,
make sure all the roads are clean and safe, and that's being done. But just please continue to
exercise caution in the next couple of days. The remnants of Isaias are moving across the southeast
with the risk of flash flooding. Debbie Elliott, NPR News, Questview, Florida.
Police in Erie, Pennsylvania are investigating a mass shooting overnight that left multiple people
dead after a gunman opened fire at a home. Authorities say the shooter is also dead.
Erie Police Chief Rick Laura. This is one of the most difficult and heartbreaking scenes our
officers and investigators have ever encountered. The loss of life is devastating and the circumstances
we are working through are deeply disturbing. At this time, we can confirm that the suspect is
deceased. Based on the information currently available to us, there is no ongoing threat to
the public. So far, there's no word on a motive. Consumer spending kept rising in September.
That's according to the Bank of America Institute and based on consumer spending data.
NPR's Stephen Besaha reports lower-income households though saw some of the fastest
spending growth. Overall, spending grew 6.2 percent compared with last September.
The Bank of America Institute's David Tinsley said bad vibes about the economy have not stopped
shoppers. Spending is remarkably resilient for consumers. Spending growth by lower-income
households has outpaced all but the highest earners. That's a change from how much they
lagged other groups earlier this year and last. That is probably the single biggest
change we've seen in our data, say over the last three or four months.
Spending growth is outpacing inflation and growing faster than it was at this time last year,
both for essential and discretionary items. Stephen Besaha, NPR News, Birmingham, Alabama.
Just weeks ahead of the midterm elections, President Trump continues to campaign for
Republican candidates in GOP-friendly states. Today, he'll be in Tennessee where he'll be
touting his economic agenda and he also credits his tariffs with economic growth.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington. India is stepping up its police deployment
ahead of protests against the country's election commission chief. NPR's Omkar Kandekar has more.
The popular youth group, Kokrojanta Party, has announced a sit-in demanding the resignation
of the election chief after more than 100 million names were deleted from India's voter lists.
Authorities have cut off the Internet, shut dozens of metro stations,
and put up barricades in parts of New Delhi. The police have also put up loudspeakers,
warning people not to protest and telling journalists not to get in their way.
The clampdown comes a week after protests by citizens and India's opposition parties.
They accuse India's election commission of rigging the voter lists to favor Prime Minister
Narendra Modi. Authorities expect protests to try to escalate over the weekend,
but they say they won't allow it. Omkar Kandekar, NPR News, New Delhi.
Families headed by a person aged 75 years or older are now America's wealthiest,
while the youngest families saw their wealth decline in the past three years.
This all thanks to steady gains in the stock market. That's according to the Federal Reserve
Survey of Consumer Finances, and it underscores how robust stock market gains have made wealthier
American families even richer since the survey conducted every three years was last completed in 2022.
I'm Janine Herbst, and you're listening to NPR News from Washington.

topics.text: Hurricane Isaias makes landfall near Destin, Florida, leaving hundreds of thousands without power and two dead
Erie, Pennsylvania police investigate overnight mass shooting at a home that left multiple people dead, shooter also dead
Bank of America Institute reports consumer spending rose 6.2 percent in September, with lower-income households leading growth
President Trump campaigns in Tennessee for Republican candidates ahead of the midterm elections
India deploys police and cuts internet ahead of youth group protest against election chief over deleted voter names
